before.title: The intake pilot
before.content:
<!-- layout: title; theme: editorial; design: v1 -->
# The intake pilot

A shorter review cycle, with an unanswered quality question. [1][2]

---

<!-- layout: composed -->
<!-- scene:  -->
## The pilot measured time; quality remains unknown [1][2]

In this synthetic intake pilot, median review time was 40 hours before the pilot and 16 hours during the pilot. The observation covered two teams over eight weeks. These are training data, not actual organizational results. [1]

The two-team intake pilot did not measure review quality or error rates. A faster review cannot establish a quality improvement. The sample does not establish an effect in other teams. [2]

beforeFindings.problem: The first body paragraph's citation marker "[1]" wraps onto a line by itself below the paragraph, leaving a stranded superscript and an extra ragged blank line before the second paragraph.
beforeFindings.correction: Tighten the paragraph so the citation stays attached to its last sentence — e.g. condense "The observation covered two teams over eight weeks." into the preceding sentence — or move the [1] marker to the end of the second paragraph. Keep "These are training data, not actual organizational results." intact.

beforeFindings.problem: The page carries both messages at once: a two-line heading plus two dense 32pt paragraphs covering the time result and the measurement gap, filling the frame to its lower margin (flagged as not fitting at a readable size). Neither the time result nor the limitation gets visual emphasis.
beforeFindings.correction: Split across two slides: one showing the time result (40h median before, 16h during, two teams over eight weeks, training data only) and one stating what was not measured and why that gap blocks a decision.
